why: Rewriting C5 changed the model’s severity signal so its top-ranked cuts shifted (rank_depth shows clear gains at depths 1–2) but cuts deeper in the list became less faithful (depths 3–5 drop). Concretely the model began proposing earlier/high-ranked splits that separate punctuation/quotes and sometimes cut inside multi-character nominal modifiers (the worst examples), which produced a small net harm concentrated in long-latency bins even though the very top positions improved.
lesson: Keep the severity wording from signaling that internal characters of multi-character nominals are acceptable cut points—preserve modifier+head integrity for deeper-ranked cuts while only adjusting how immediately-post-modifier cuts are scored.
